title: Who Wins the Game of Noughts and Crosses?

concept.title: Minimax: each player picks the best move for themselves
body: In a two-player game with a win, a loss or a draw, the value of a position is found by looking at **all moves**: the player to move chooses the move that is best for them, and the opponent will answer with their best move. Give the value `+1` when `X` wins, `-1` when `O` wins and `0` for a draw. `X` takes the **maximum** over all moves, `O` takes the **minimum**.

body.code:
def value(b, turn, memo):               # b is a string of 9 characters
    if b in memo:
        return memo[b]
    w = winner(b)
    if w == "X": result = 1
    elif w == "O": result = -1
    elif "." not in b: result = 0           # a full board without a winner
    else:
        results = [value(b[:i] + turn + b[i + 1:], "O" if turn == "X" else "X", memo)
                   for i in range(9) if b[i] == "."]
        result = max(results) if turn == "X" else min(results)
    memo[b] = result
    return result

body: This is backtracking in a new role: the search tree is the tree of **all possible games**, and the values come up from the leaves. There are 5478 different positions (many games lead to the same one), so a memo on the board text makes the search very fast. The player to move is known from the numbers of X and O on the board, so the board alone is a good key.

statement: Noughts and crosses is played on a 3 by 3 board. The players `X` and `O` write their sign in an empty cell in turn. The game stops as soon as a player has three signs in a row, column or diagonal (that player wins), or when the board is full (a draw). A position and the player who moves next are given. Both players play perfectly. Print `X` if `X` wins, `O` if `O` wins, or `draw`.
inputFormat: The first 3 lines have the board: `X`, `O` or `.` (empty).
The fourth line has the player to move: `X` or `O`.
constraints: The position is reachable in a real game: the player who moves next has made the same number of moves as the other, or one fewer; if a player has already won, that player is the answer.

examples.note: X moves and plays the bottom left cell to make three in a column: X wins.

hints: Give a position the value 1, 0 or -1 and let X maximise it and O minimise it.
A position with a winner or a full board is a leaf of the search.
Positions repeat: store the value of each board text in a dictionary.

starter.python:

explanation: A position is a leaf when someone has three in a row or the board is full. Otherwise X takes the maximum and O the minimum of the values of the positions after each possible move; a dictionary stores each position once.
solution.complexity: Time O(5478 * 9) positions at most, space O(5478).
